finding.claim: The dumb-HTTP object fetch decompresses the entire server response with zlib.decompress() and no output cap, so a malicious server can serve a small zlib stream that expands to gigabytes and exhaust the client's memory during clone/fetch.
finding.source: HTTP response body for objects/<xx>/<38 hex> served by an attacker-controlled remote. The dumb protocol is selected when the info/refs response lacks an application/x-git-* Content-Type (client.py:4577-4580), so a plain HTTP server is enough.
finding.sink: zlib.decompress(compressed) at dulwich/dumb.py:144, which allocates the full decompressed output before any size or header check.

trace.note: Object path built from the requested sha (hex-only in practice)
compressed = self._fetch_url(path) reads the whole body
_fetch_url accumulates read(4096) chunks into an unbounded list (lines 432-436)
zlib.decompress with no max_length; deflate ratios of roughly 1000:1 let a few MB expand to GB
Declared obj_size is only parsed after decompression, so it cannot bound the allocation

finding.guards_checked: Status-code checks only (404/200 in _fetch_url). No Content-Length or body-size cap on the read. No zlib max_length. Declared object size is parsed only after decompression. The smart-HTTP and LFS paths were checked separately and do not share this sink. Severity: low (client DoS, no code execution). Not reproduced at runtime.

finding.claim: On macOS with default config, the HFS-ignorable .git check is never used, because core.protectNTFS defaults to true and short-circuits the HFS branch. The NTFS validator does not strip HFS ignorable code points, so a tree entry such as '.g‌it/config' passes validation and can be written into the real .git directory on HFS+-style volumes.
finding.source: Tree entry name in an attacker-authored repository being checked out (clone or checkout of an untrusted repo).
finding.sink: build_index_from_tree writes the blob to root/<name> (index.py:2229-2253 via build_file_from_blob). On a filesystem that folds U+200C, the path resolves to .git/config, which can set core.fsmonitor, core.sshCommand or core.hooksPath and lead to command execution the next time git runs in that repo.

trace.note: update_working_tree derives the validator from config when none is passed
get_path_element_validator: protectNTFS defaults True, so the NTFS validator is returned and the protectHFS/darwin branch (2165-2166) is unreachable by default, contrary to the docstring at 2150-2152
validate_path_element_ntfs: _is_ntfs_dotgit (2031-2056) compares ASCII bytes, so b'.g\xe2\x80\x8cit' does not match
_normalize_path_element_ntfs only does rstrip(b'. ').lower(), with no HFS_IGNORABLE_CHARS removal (those are used only in _normalize_path_element_hfs at 1943-1954)
validate_path is called per entry, and the element passes
build_file_from_blob writes the file at the unvalidated-spelling path

finding.guards_checked: validate_path (index.py:2171) with the NTFS validator (dot-git, reserved device names, INVALID_DOTNAMES). Git's own is_hfs_dotgit logic is not implemented on this default path. The HFS validator is never reached unless core.protectNTFS=false is set explicitly. Verdict: PLAUSIBLE. Exploitability depends on the target volume folding U+200C (classic HFS+ does; modern APFS behavior was not verified here). The checkout path itself is otherwise sound (default validator rejects .git/./..).
